# SOP-P1-L1-04 Shift handover - Hot Forge line

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Purpose
1. Provide a consistent, auditable handover procedure for shift-to-shift transfer of responsibility on the Hot Forge line (P1-L1), minimizing safety and production risk and ensuring continuity of maintenance actions.

Scope
2. Applies to operators, lead technicians, and supervisors assigned to EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 during normal production shifts.

Preconditions
3. Shift incoming and outgoing personnel have completed site access and induction training per SOP-P1-L1-01.  
4. Any active maintenance or intervention on EQ-P1-L1-IH03 referenced in MM-P1-L1-IH03 must be documented and the status communicated during handover.  
5. Control room and shop floor communications are functional; any failure must be escalated before completing the handover.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
6. Minimum PPE required for handover walkthroughs at the Hot Forge line: hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves, safety glasses, high-visibility garment, and steel-toe footwear. Any additional PPE required for a specific task must be noted in SOP-P1-L1-02 and observed.

Handover procedure (numbered steps)
7. Outgoing shift preparation
   7.1. Review the shift log for EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and EQ-P1-L1-IH03 and summarize open items, completed actions, and any deviations.  
   7.2. Verify that lubricant stock levels and part numbers for critical lubrication points are recorded. Explicitly confirm that the lubricant part number for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is CFW-LUB-188 and that the lubricant part number for Hot Forge CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P1-L1-CN02) is CFW-LUB-508. Note any discrepancies for follow-up.  
   7.3. Ensure that any tools, fixtures, and portable equipment placed in service are accounted for and stored per site practice.

8. Joint walkthrough and verbal transfer
   8.1. Conduct a floor walkthrough with outgoing and incoming personnel together, covering EQ-P1-L1-RR01, EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and EQ-P1-L1-IH03. Use the printed shift log as the working document.  
   8.2. For each machine, communicate status items including current job, scrap or quality concerns, known faults, temporary guards or bypasses, and required follow-up actions. Use clear, specific language and confirm understanding by asking the incoming operator to repeat safety-critical items.  
   8.3. Where maintenance remains outstanding, reference MM-P1-L1-IH03 for EQ-P1-L1-IH03-related maintenance history and outstanding tasks. Confirm whether equipment is available for production or is locked/tagged out.

9. Records and documentation
   9.1. Update the shift log with a concise summary of handover contents, including open actions, responsible person for follow-up, and the time of transfer. Retain the completed log in accordance with site record retention practice.  
   9.2. Record any lubricant usage events or replenishments against the equipment record, making explicit entries for CFW-LUB-188 and CFW-LUB-508 when used. Attach purchase requisition or stock issuance records as required.  
   9.3. If any non-routine intervention is performed, create or update a maintenance request and reference MM-P1-L1-IH03 where relevant.

10. Examples and clarifications
   10.1. Example: If EQ-P1-L1-IH03 shows intermittent temperature control instability and a technician has scheduled a sensor verification, the outgoing operator notes the open work in the shift log, references MM-P1-L1-IH03, confirms lock/tag status if applicable, and states the technician assigned. The incoming operator acknowledges and signs the handover.  
   10.2. Example: If EQ-P1-L1-CN02 requires lubrication, the outgoing operator documents the lubricant used (CFW-LUB-508), the quantity taken from stock, and the location serviced. Records are attached to the shift log.

11. Rationale and expected outcomes
   11.1. Structured, verbal-plus-documented handovers reduce missed actions and latent hazards. Explicit naming of lubricant part numbers for equipment removes ambiguity in replenishment and maintenance records.  
   11.2. Joint walkthroughs provide a chance to observe latent issues and reinforce safe behaviors; documented follow-up prevents repeated interruptions to production while ensuring safety defects are addressed.

12. Escalation
   12.1. If the incoming operator does not accept the handover due to unresolved safety concerns, stop production activity related to the hazard and escalate to the on-duty supervisor per SOP-P1-L1-02.

Sign-off
13. The outgoing operator, incoming operator, and on-duty supervisor must sign the shift log. The sign-off must include printed name, signature, and a short acknowledgement that the incoming operator was briefed on open safety items, lubricant status including explicit confirmation of CFW-LUB-188 for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 and CFW-LUB-508 for EQ-P1-L1-CN02, and any active maintenance per MM-P1-L1-IH03.

Records to keep
14. - Completed shift log with sign-offs.  
    - Lubricant issuance or usage records that reference CFW-LUB-188 and CFW-LUB-508.  
    - Any maintenance requests or completed work orders tied to MM-P1-L1-IH03.  
    - Exception reports and incident forms per SOP-P1-L1-02.

Related documents
15. - MM-P1-L1-IH03  
    - SOP-P1-L1-01  
    - SOP-P1-L1-02

Revision control
16. Rev A: initial controlled release.
